---
title: "R code to generate Kaplan-Meier graph"
output: html_document
params:
    ordinal_data: NA
    no_dose: NA
    toxicA: NA
    baseA: NA
    ordinal_date: NA
    graphtitle: NA
    titlesize: NA
    axissize: 30
    x_lab: "Time"
    y_lab: NA
    box_x: -0.5
    box_y: 0.05
---

```{r}
print(params[-2])

## To install the required packages, uncomment the following lines and run the code
# install.packages(c("ggplot2", "DT", "magrittr", "dplyr", "ggsurvfit", "ggh4x", "tidyr", "gt", "gridExtra", "survminer"))
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggsurvfit)
library(ggh4x)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)
library(gridExtra)
library(survminer)

# Function to handle date data
date_to_timepoint_ordinal <- function(data) {
    data %>%
        group_by(id, toxicity) %>%
        arrange(timepoint) %>%
        mutate(date = timepoint, timepoint = row_number() - 1) %>%
        ungroup()
}


# Select the data for the specified dose and toxicity
summary_df <- params$ordinal_data %>%
    filter(dose %in% params$no_dose) %>%
    filter(toxicity %in% params$toxicA)


# To read in the data, uncomment the following line and add in the filepath to your data file after ensuring it meets the app formatting requirements.
# ordinal_data <- read.csv(FILEPATH, header = TRUE, sep = ",")
# Also ensure that the next line is commented out if you are reading in your own data file.
ordinal_data <- params$ordinal_data

# Calculates the baseline adjusted grade for each patient and toxicity
if (params$ordinal_date == TRUE) {
    ordinal_formatted <- ordinal_data %>%
        date_to_timepoint_ordinal()
    ordinal_data$base_adj <- ordinal_formatted %>%
        group_by(id, toxicity) %>%
        mutate(base_adj = grade - grade[timepoint == min(ordinal_formatted$timepoint)]) %>%
        select(base_adj) %>%
        pull()
} else {
    ordinal_data <- ordinal_data %>%
        group_by(id, toxicity) %>%
        mutate(base_adj = grade - grade[timepoint == min(ordinal_data$timepoint)])
}

# Filter out rows with NA values (remove patients with missing baseline adjusted grade)
ordinal_data <- ordinal_data %>% filter(is.na(base_adj) == FALSE)

change <- params$baseA

# Create a summary dataframe with time to event and event occurrence for each patient
if (params$ordinal_date == TRUE) {
    summary_df <- ordinal_data %>%
        group_by(id) %>%
        summarise(
            time = if (any(base_adj >= change)) as.numeric(min(as.Date(timepoint[base_adj >= change])) - min(as.Date(timepoint))) else as.numeric(max(as.Date(timepoint)) - min(as.Date(timepoint))),
            event = as.integer(any(base_adj >= change))
        )
} else {
    summary_df <- ordinal_data %>%
        group_by(id) %>%
        summarise(
            time = if (any(base_adj >= change)) as.numeric(min(timepoint[base_adj >= change]) - min(timepoint)) else as.numeric(max(timepoint) - min(timepoint)),
            event = as.integer(any(base_adj >= change))
        )
}

# Add the dose to the summary dataframe and name it "dose"
summary_df <- cbind(summary_df, ordinal_data %>% group_by(id) %>% dplyr::summarise(max(dose)))
colnames(summary_df)[5] <- "dose"

# Create a survfit object to be used to plot a Kaplan-Meier graph and calculate median time to event for each dose group
fit <- survfit2(Surv(time, event) ~ dose, data = summary_df)

median_df <- survminer::surv_median(fit) %>%
    dplyr::select(strata, median) %>%
    rename(Dose = strata, "Median time \n to event" = median)

median_df[, 1] <- paste0("Dose: ", unique(summary_df$dose))

# Create a tableGrob object to display the median time to event for each dose group
tbl_grob <- tableGrob(median_df,
    rows = NULL,
    theme = ttheme_default(
        core = list(
            fg_params = list(cex = 0.7, col = "black"),
            bg_params = list(fill = NA, col = "black")
        ),
        colhead = list(
            fg_params = list(cex = 0.8, fontface = "bold", col = "black"),
            bg_params = list(fill = NA, col = "black")
        )
    )
)

summary_df$dose <- paste0("Dose: ", summary_df$dose)

# Create the Kaplan-Meier graph
survfit2(Surv(time, event) ~ dose, data = summary_df) %>%
    ggsurvfit(linewidth = 1.5) +
    add_censor_mark() +
    add_confidence_interval() +
    scale_ggsurvfit() + add_risktable() +
    ggtitle(params$graphtitle) + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = params$titlesize, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = params$axissize)) +
    labs(y = params$y_lab, x = params$x_lab) +
    annotation_custom(
        tbl_grob,
        xmin = params$box_x, xmax = params$box_x + 2, # x-position range for table
        ymin = params$box_y, ymax = params$box_y + 0.3 # y-position range for table
    )
```
